stem:
Pallavi works out $\dfrac{5}{6} \div \dfrac{3}{4}$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Keep $\dfrac{5}{6}$ and multiply by $\dfrac{3}{4}$ directly, with no reciprocal of the divisor.
Treat the reciprocal $\dfrac{4}{3}$ as choosing the original divisor $\dfrac{3}{4}$, instead of multiplying the dividend by that reciprocal.
Swap the fractions and write $\dfrac{3}{4} \div \dfrac{5}{6}$, as if division order did not matter.

teacher.key_rationale: To divide by $\dfrac{3}{4}$, multiply by its reciprocal $\dfrac{4}{3}$: $\dfrac{5}{6}\times\dfrac{4}{3}=\dfrac{10}{9}$. Skipping the reciprocal, reversing reciprocal and divisor, or swapping division order all miss that hinge.
